# Lumiose UI

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

These docs ship in `@lumiose/ui` and match the installed version: `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`.
In a project that depends on it, `lumiose docs ui` prints the index and `lumiose docs dialog` a
component's page; the Lumiose MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists every component's parts,
props, events and styling hooks. The Lumiose docs: `node_modules/lumiose/docs/llms.txt`.

<!-- source: README.md -->

# UI components

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

**Status:** in development. `@lumiose/ui` keeps its own 0.x versions, apart from the version all
other Lumiose packages share, and is not on npm yet: today it is used from this repository's
workspace. The goal for its 1.0 is parity with [Base UI](https://base-ui.com)'s components; the
table below lists them as they land.

These pages ship in the package, in `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`, so they match the installed
version. For coding agents, `llms.txt` indexes them and `llms-full.txt` holds them all;
`lumiose docs ui` and `lumiose docs dialog` print them; the MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists
every component's parts, props, events and styling hooks; and `lumiose agents init` adds a UI
section to `AGENTS.md` and the `lumiose-ui` skill. Every component page has the same sections:
Anatomy, API, Example, Styling, Keyboard and focus, Without JavaScript, Browser support and Related.

## Approach

- **Native first.** A component renders the element the platform already has for the job: a
  `<dialog>` opened by an invoker command, a popover, a `<button>`. Those work in server HTML
  before any script loads, and keep the browser's own keyboard handling and focus management.
- **Custom elements only where the platform falls short.** Keyboard navigation in a menu or the
  filtering of a combobox need script: those components render a light-DOM custom element with a
  `lu-` tag (`lu-menu`, `lu-combobox`) that upgrades the server HTML in place. A page is meant to
  load only the definitions of the elements it renders, and no island runtime for them (in
  development, with those components).
- **Small scripts for native gaps.** Where a native element falls short of Base UI's behaviour, a
  small script closes the gap, such as Dialog's right-click and touch handling. The component
  still works without it; a page that renders the component loads it once, without the island
  runtime.
- **Parts.** Each component is a set of parts named as in Base UI (`Dialog.Root`,
  `Dialog.Trigger`, `Dialog.Popup`, …). Every part that renders an element takes that element's
  props (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, events) and passes them through.
- **Signals.** A component's state is a prop and a callback: `open` with `onOpenChange`, `checked`
  with `onCheckedChange`, `value` with `onValueChange`. Pass a signal's value and write it back in
  the callback to keep both in sync, or leave both out and the element keeps its own state. Custom
  elements report changes with lowercase DOM events, like native ones: `openchange`,
  `checkedchange` and `change`.
- **Keyboard contracts.** Every component follows its WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern, and
  its end-to-end tests check the keyboard paths and run axe.

This is the approach of [Timeless](https://timeless.build), ported to Lumiose.

## Styling

`@lumiose/ui` is **unstyled**: its stylesheets hold only what a component needs to work
(display, positioning and anchoring, the top layer, the CSS variables a component sets), in the
`lu.core` cascade layer. A look is opt-in: the default theme, or your own CSS.

```ts
import "@lumiose/ui/styles.css"; // what every component needs (or "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css", …)
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

Both stylesheets declare the layers `lu.core, lu.theme`, in that order. CSS outside layers always
wins over layered CSS, so your own stylesheets override the package's without specificity games.
If your app orders its own layers, put `lu` first: `@layer lu, reset, components;`.

### The default theme

`@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css` is a ready look for demos, prototypes and getting started: neutral
surfaces, a blue primary, light and dark. It styles a few classes, which you put on the parts
through their `class` prop:

| Class       | On                  | Variants                                                                |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lu-button` | any `<button>` part | `data-variant="primary"`, `data-variant="destructive"`                  |
| `lu-dialog` | `Dialog.Popup`      | Styles the backdrop, the title, the description and a `<footer>` inside |

Its colours and radius are custom properties with shadcn/ui's names and a `--lu-` prefix, so a
shadcn palette carries over:

| Property                                          | Used for                            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `--lu-background`, `--lu-foreground`              | Page-level surfaces and text        |
| `--lu-card`, `--lu-card-foreground`               | Cards                               |
| `--lu-popover`, `--lu-popover-foreground`         | Dialogs, popovers, menus            |
| `--lu-primary`, `--lu-primary-foreground`         | Primary actions                     |
| `--lu-secondary`, `--lu-secondary-foreground`     | Secondary actions                   |
| `--lu-muted`, `--lu-muted-foreground`             | Subdued surfaces and text           |
| `--lu-accent`, `--lu-accent-foreground`           | Hover and highlighted items         |
| `--lu-destructive`, `--lu-destructive-foreground` | Destructive actions                 |
| `--lu-border`, `--lu-input`, `--lu-ring`          | Borders, field borders, focus rings |
| `--lu-radius`                                     | Corner radius                       |

The theme sets `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` and every colour with `light-dark()`, so it
follows the system. Set `color-scheme: light` (or `dark`) on `:root` or on any element to force
one, and redefine a property outside layers to change it:

```css
:root {
  --lu-primary: #7c3aed;
  --lu-radius: 0.375rem;
}
```

### Your own CSS

Style the parts through:

- **Class props.** Every part takes `class` (and `style`), like the element it renders. No part
  carries a class or attribute of its own.
- **State.** Components expose state the way the platform does, so selectors read it directly:
  `dialog[open]`, `:modal`, `::backdrop`, `:popover-open`, `[aria-expanded]`, `[aria-checked]`,
  `[aria-selected]`, and `data-highlighted` on the active option of a list.

Each component's page has an example stylesheet to start from.

## Components

| Component                         | Status                                                 |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| [Dialog, alert dialog](dialog.md) | Available: native `<dialog>`, works without JavaScript |
| Popover, tooltip                  | Planned                                                |
| [Menu](menu.md)                   | Available: popover menu, opens without JavaScript      |
| Combobox, select                  | Planned                                                |
| Tabs                              | Planned                                                |

## Size

`@lumiose/ui` is opt-in, so its size is reported apart from the runtime's caps:
`pnpm --filter @lumiose/ui size` prints, per component, the JavaScript a server-rendered page loads
for its custom elements, the JavaScript an island that uses it loads, and its CSS (minified, gzip
and brotli).

## Related

- [Web components](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/guides/web-components/): custom elements in Lumiose pages and islands.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): where components run in the browser.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `class`, events and `on:`.

<!-- source: dialog.md -->

# Dialog

> A modal dialog, or an alert dialog that needs an answer: a native `<dialog>` opened and closed by invoker commands, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 0.8 kB script closes the native element's gaps where JavaScript runs. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/dialog"
import "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css"; // locks the page's scroll behind a modal dialog
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog.Root>
  <Dialog.Trigger />
  <Dialog.Popup>
    <Dialog.Title />
    <Dialog.Description />
    <Dialog.Close />
  </Dialog.Popup>
</Dialog.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | No element. Holds the state and the ids the other parts share.                                                                |
| `Trigger`     | `<button type="button" command="show-modal" commandfor="…" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="…">`                         |
| `Popup`       | `<dialog closedby="…">`, labelled by its `Title` and described by its `Description`; `role="alertdialog"` for an alert dialog |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`, which names the dialog.                                                                                               |
| `Description` | `<p>`, which describes it.                                                                                                    |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" command="close" commandfor="…">`: its `value` becomes the dialog's `returnValue`.                      |

The trigger can sit anywhere inside `Root`, and a popup may have several close buttons. `Title` and
`Description` go inside `Popup`. A dialog may contain another `Dialog.Root`: the inner dialog
opens on top of the outer one.

## API

### Dialog.Root

| Prop           | Type                        | Default    |                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | --------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                   |            | Opens or closes the dialog when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a modal dialog opens only from a trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`   |            | Called after the dialog opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a close button, Escape, a click outside or `open`.                         |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`           |            | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`: the signal opens and closes the dialog, and follows it.                                                  |
| `role`         | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog"` | `"dialog"` | `"alertdialog"` for a confirmation that needs an answer: a click outside does not close it.                                                       |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the dialog keeps its own state.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`,
`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `closedby`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`); `id`,
`command` and `commandfor` stay the parts' own, since they connect the parts.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` follows the dialog in the browser. In server HTML it stays
  `"false"`, which is never wrong where assistive technology can reach it: while the modal dialog
  is open, the trigger is inert.
- **`Popup`**: `closedby` is `"any"` for a dialog (Escape or a click outside closes it) and
  `"closerequest"` for an alert dialog (Escape only); pass `closedby="none"` to allow neither. Native
  events work as on a `<dialog>`: `on:close` runs after any close, and
  `event.currentTarget.returnValue` holds the value of the `Close` that closed it (it is unchanged
  after Escape).
- **`Title`** and **`Description`**: the popup's `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` point at
  the ones it renders, and only those; in an island they follow parts that appear or go away. A
  dialog without a `Title` needs an `aria-label` on `Popup`.

## Example

A confirmation in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog.Root role="alertdialog">
      <Dialog.Trigger class="lu-button">Delete project…</Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Popup class="lu-dialog">
        <Dialog.Title>Delete project?</Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description>This removes the project and its deployments.</Dialog.Description>
        <footer>
          <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" value="cancel">
            Cancel
          </Dialog.Close>
          <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="destructive" value="delete">
            Delete
          </Dialog.Close>
        </footer>
      </Dialog.Popup>
    </Dialog.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: the button outside opens it, and the signal follows whatever
closes it. `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}` plus
`onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function EditProfile() {
  const open = signal(false);
  const saved = signal("");
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" onClick={() => open.set(true)}>
        Edit profile
      </button>
      <Dialog.Root bind:open={open}>
        <Dialog.Popup
          class="lu-dialog"
          on:close={(event) => saved.set(event.currentTarget.returnValue)}
        >
          <Dialog.Title>Edit profile</Dialog.Title>
          <Dialog.Description>Your name as others see it.</Dialog.Description>
          <footer>
            <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="primary" value="save">
              Save
            </Dialog.Close>
          </footer>
        </Dialog.Popup>
      </Dialog.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "Editing…" : `Last answer: ${saved() || "none"}`}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-dialog` on `Popup` and `lu-button` on the buttons
(`data-variant="primary"` or `"destructive"` for filled ones). `lu-dialog` also styles the backdrop,
the title, the description and a `<footer>` for the buttons, and fades and zooms the dialog in and
out. Its colours come from the theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)).

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and the dialog's native state: `dialog[open]`,
`:modal`, `::backdrop` and `[role="alertdialog"]`. Where the client script runs, a dialog with open
dialogs inside also gets `data-nested-dialog-open` and `--nested-dialogs` (how many are open inside
it), as in Base UI; `dialog:has(dialog[open])` matches the same dialogs without the script. A starting point, with a fade that keeps the dialog in the top layer while it
closes:

```css
.dialog {
  inline-size: min(28rem, 100vw - 2rem);
  padding: 1.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.75rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
}
.dialog::backdrop {
  background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  .dialog,
  .dialog::backdrop {
    transition:
      opacity 150ms ease-out,
      overlay 150ms allow-discrete,
      display 150ms allow-discrete;
  }
  .dialog:not([open]),
  .dialog:not([open])::backdrop {
    opacity: 0;
  }
  @starting-style {
    .dialog[open],
    .dialog[open]::backdrop {
      opacity: 0;
    }
  }
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/dialog.css` holds one rule, in the `lu.core` layer: the page behind any modal
`<dialog>` does not scroll, and keeps its scrollbar's space so the layout does not shift
(`:root:has(dialog:modal) { overflow: hidden; scrollbar-gutter: stable }`). Leave the stylesheet out,
or override the rule, to let the page scroll.

## Keyboard and focus

The browser's modal dialog provides the
[WAI-ARIA dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/):

| Key            | Does                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space   | On the trigger: opens the dialog.                                                                    |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Move between the focusable elements of the dialog. The page behind is inert: focus never reaches it. |
| Escape         | Closes the dialog on top, alert dialogs included. With nested dialogs, one Escape closes one dialog. |

- **On open**, focus moves to the element with `autofocus`, or else the first focusable element
  inside, or else the dialog. Opened by touch, the dialog focuses itself instead, so no virtual
  keyboard opens over it (an `autofocus` element still gets focus).
- **On close**, focus returns to the element that had it before: the trigger, or the button that
  set the signal. If that element is gone, focus goes to another trigger of the dialog, without
  scrolling the page.
- **A click outside** closes a dialog, not an alert dialog, and only the dialog on top. A press
  that starts inside and ends outside, such as selecting text, does not count, and neither does a
  right-click or a second finger.
- Popups opened from a dialog (a menu, a select) belong inside its `Popup`: everything outside a
  modal dialog is inert.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger, the close buttons, Escape and the click outside are HTML features: a dialog in a
server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none. `open`, `onOpenChange`,
`bind:open` and a live `aria-expanded` need the component to run in the browser, in an island.

Where the native element falls short of Base UI's dialog, a small script closes the gap: a page
that renders a `Dialog` loads it once, as a 0.8 kB (brotli) module without the Lumiose runtime, and
islands bundle it. It covers every `<dialog>` on the page:

- a right-click or a second finger outside does not close the dialog;
- `data-nested-dialog-open` and `--nested-dialogs` on a dialog with open dialogs inside;
- a dialog opened by touch focuses itself;
- focus returns without scrolling, to the opener or, if it is gone, another trigger (WebKit, which
  does not focus a clicked button, would otherwise leave focus on the page);
- the click outside where the browser lacks `closedby` (Safari), and the invoker commands where it
  lacks them.

Until the script loads (or without JavaScript) the dialog behaves as the browser's own.

## Browser support

- **Invoker commands** (`command`, `commandfor`) open and close the dialog: Chrome and Edge 135,
  Firefox 144, Safari 26.2. In older browsers the client script stands in for them; without
  JavaScript the trigger and the close buttons do nothing there.
- **`closedby`**: Chrome 134 and Firefox 141; Safari only in Technology Preview. Elsewhere the
  client script closes the dialog on a click outside; without JavaScript only Escape does.
- **Exit animations** that keep the dialog in the top layer (`overlay`) are Chromium-only.
  Elsewhere the dialog leaves the top layer as soon as it starts closing.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the browser, for `open` and
  `onOpenChange`.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): native events with `on:` and `ref`.

<!-- source: menu.md -->

# Menu

> A menu of commands, links, checkbox and radio items and submenus, opened by a button: the trigger's `popovertarget` opens it and CSS anchor positioning places it, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 2.4 kB script adds the APG Menu Button keyboard contract where JavaScript runs. `bind:open`, `bind:checked` and `bind:value` keep signals in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/menu"
import "@lumiose/ui/menu.css"; // places the popup next to its trigger and stacks the items
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger />
  <Menu.Popup>
    <Menu.Item />
    <Menu.LinkItem />
    <Menu.CheckboxItem />
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Group>
      <Menu.GroupLabel />
      <Menu.Item />
    </Menu.Group>
    <Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.GroupLabel />
      <Menu.RadioItem />
    </Menu.RadioGroup>
    <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      <Menu.SubmenuTrigger />
      <Menu.Popup>…</Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
  </Menu.Popup>
</Menu.Root>
```

| Part             | Renders                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`           | `<lu-menu>`, an element with no box (`display: contents`) that holds the menu's state and adds the keyboard contract.                                |
| `Trigger`        | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="menu">`; `aria-expanded` follows the menu once the script runs.                              |
| `Popup`          | `<div role="menu" popover="auto" tabindex="-1" data-side="…" data-align="…">`, labelled by its trigger; `popover="manual"` once the script opens it. |
| `Item`           | `<button type="button" role="menuitem">`: a command.                                                                                                 |
| `LinkItem`       | `<a role="menuitem">`: a link.                                                                                                                       |
| `CheckboxItem`   | `<button type="button" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="…">`                                                                                    |
| `Separator`      | `<div role="separator">`                                                                                                                             |
| `Group`          | `<div role="group">`, labelled by its `GroupLabel`.                                                                                                  |
| `GroupLabel`     | `<div role="presentation">`, which names its `Group` or `RadioGroup`.                                                                                |
| `RadioGroup`     | `<div role="group">` of radio items, one of them checked.                                                                                            |
| `RadioItem`      | `<button type="button" role="menuitemradio" value="…" aria-checked="…">`                                                                             |
| `SubmenuRoot`    | `<lu-menu>` for a submenu, inside a `Popup`.                                                                                                         |
| `SubmenuTrigger` | `<button type="button" role="menuitem" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="menu">`: an item of the parent menu.                                         |

The trigger and the popup sit inside `Root`; a submenu's trigger and popup sit inside its
`SubmenuRoot`, which sits in the parent's `Popup`, as deep as you like. Items, groups and separators
go inside a `Popup`, radio items inside a `RadioGroup`.

## API

### Menu.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the menu when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a popover opens only from its trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the menu opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a key, a click outside, an item that ran, `open`.                       |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`: the signal opens and closes the menu, and follows it.                                               |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the menu keeps its own state. A menu opened from the
server HTML before its island hydrated stays open, and `onOpenChange(true)` tells the signal.
`Menu.SubmenuRoot` takes the same props, for its submenu.

### Menu.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default                                 |                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"`, `"inline-end"` in a submenu | The trigger's side the popup goes on. It flips when it does not fit. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"start"`                               | How the popup aligns with the trigger along that side.               |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   |                                         | The gap between the trigger and the popup, in CSS pixels.            |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   |                                         | A shift along the side, away from the aligned edge, in CSS pixels.   |

### Menu.Item

| Prop           | Type                          | Default |                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onClick`      | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |         | Runs the command, on a click, Enter or Space. The menu has closed and focus is back on the trigger by then. |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                     | `false` | Unavailable (`aria-disabled`): the arrows and typeahead still reach it, but it does not run.                |
| `label`        | `string`                      |         | The text typeahead matches, when the item's text content is not it.                                         |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean`                     | `true`  | Whether running the item closes the menu.                                                                   |

### Menu.LinkItem

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`         | `string`  |         | Where the link goes. A Ctrl, Cmd or Shift click, or a link with `download`, leaves the menu open.                                                                            |
| `label`        | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `true`  | Whether following the link closes the menu. Base UI keeps it open by default; here it closes, like the other items, since a layout's menu outlives a client-side navigation. |

### Menu.CheckboxItem

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                    |         | Checks or unchecks the item when it changes. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it starts checked when `checked` is left out.                        |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |         | Called after a click, Enter or Space checks or unchecks it.                  |
| `bind:checked`    | `Signal<boolean>`            |         | Stands in for `checked` and `onCheckedChange`.                               |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but it does not toggle.                  |
| `label`           | `string`                     |         | The text typeahead matches.                                                  |
| `closeOnClick`    | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether toggling it closes the menu.                                         |

### Menu.RadioGroup

| Prop            | Type                      | Default |                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                  |         | Checks the radio item with this `value` when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                  |         | The radio item checked at first when `value` is left out.                              |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |         | Called with the `value` of the radio item a click, Enter or Space checks.              |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`          |         | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                             |

### Menu.RadioItem

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                            |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`  |         | Required: the value its group takes when it is checked.    |
| `disabled`     | `boolean` | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but it is not checked. |
| `label`        | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches.                                |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether checking it closes the menu.                       |

### Menu.SubmenuTrigger

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                    |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but its submenu does not open. |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches in the parent menu.                     |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`, `tabindex`,
`aria-labelledby`, `data-side`, `data-align`); the roles, `id`, `popovertarget` and the anchor
stay the parts' own, since they connect the parts. Your `style` is kept, after the anchor's.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` is left to the browser in server HTML, where `popovertarget`
  implies it, and set by the script once it runs. Disable it with the native `disabled`.
- **`Group`** and **`RadioGroup`**: `aria-labelledby` points at their `GroupLabel` while one
  renders; without one, give the group an `aria-label`.
- **`Separator`**: a horizontal rule between items; `aria-orientation` passes through.

**Differences from Base UI's Menu.** No `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Backdrop` or `Arrow`: the top
layer and anchor positioning replace them, and the placement props go on `Popup`. The menu is not
modal: the page keeps scrolling (the popup follows its trigger), and a press outside closes the
menu and reaches what it lands on. Items render buttons, so they run with Enter and Space without
the script. There are no indicator parts: style `[aria-checked="true"]`. Submenus open on hover
after 100 ms, which no prop changes, and the root trigger does not open on hover.

## Example

A menu in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function ProjectMenu() {
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger class="lu-button">Project</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
        <Menu.LinkItem href="/settings">Settings</Menu.LinkItem>
        <Menu.LinkItem href="/members">Members</Menu.LinkItem>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
          <Menu.SubmenuTrigger>Export</Menu.SubmenuTrigger>
          <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
            <Menu.LinkItem href="/export.csv" download>
              CSV
            </Menu.LinkItem>
            <Menu.LinkItem href="/export.json" download>
              JSON
            </Menu.LinkItem>
          </Menu.Popup>
        </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      </Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, with commands, a checkbox item and a radio group bound to signals.
`bind:checked={wrap}` is short for `checked={wrap()}` plus
`onCheckedChange={(next) => wrap.set(next)}`, and `bind:value` likewise.

```tsx check
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function EditorMenu(props: { onFormat: () => void }) {
  const wrap = signal(true);
  const indent = signal("spaces");
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger class="lu-button">View</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu" align="end">
        <Menu.Item onClick={props.onFormat}>Format document</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Item disabled>Fold all</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.CheckboxItem bind:checked={wrap}>Wrap lines</Menu.CheckboxItem>
        <Menu.RadioGroup bind:value={indent}>
          <Menu.GroupLabel>Indent with</Menu.GroupLabel>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="spaces">Spaces</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="tabs">Tabs</Menu.RadioItem>
        </Menu.RadioGroup>
      </Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-menu` on every `Popup`, submenus included, and `lu-button` on
the trigger. `lu-menu` styles the surface, the items (highlighted, disabled, focus ring), the
checkbox and radio marks, the arrow of a submenu trigger, the separators and the group labels, and
fades the popup in and out. Its colours come from the theme's `--lu-` properties
([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)), and it sets a 4px gap with `--lu-side-offset`.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state:

- the popup: `:popover-open`, `data-side` and `data-align` (where it was asked to go);
- the trigger and a submenu trigger: `[aria-expanded="true"]` while their menu is open;
- items: `[data-highlighted]` on the item that has focus (by keyboard or pointer),
  `:focus-visible`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`, and `[aria-checked="true"]` on checkbox and radio
  items;
- `[role="separator"]`, `[role="group"]` and a group label's `[role="presentation"]`.

A starting point:

```css
.menu {
  min-inline-size: 10rem;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
  --lu-side-offset: 4px;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"] {
  padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
  background: none;
  font: inherit;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"][data-highlighted] {
  background: #f4f4f5;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"][aria-disabled="true"] {
  opacity: 0.5;
}
.menu [aria-checked="true"]::before {
  content: "✓" / "";
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/menu.css` holds what the menu needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer: `lu-menu` has
no box, the popup and its groups lay the items out in a column (`display: grid`, items
`display: flex`), and, where the browser has CSS anchor positioning, the popup sits on its
`data-side` and `data-align` (`position-area`), flips when it does not fit
(`position-try-fallbacks`), and keeps the gaps of `--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`. The
`sideOffset` and `alignOffset` props set those two properties on the popup.

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/), with
Base UI's behaviour where the pattern leaves a choice:

| Key                       | Does                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space              | On the trigger: opens the menu on its first item. On an item: runs it, or checks it. On a submenu trigger: opens it. |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Up      | On the trigger: opens the menu on its first item, or on its last. In the menu: the next or previous item, looping.   |
| Home, End                 | The first or last item.                                                                                              |
| Arrow Right (Left in RTL) | On a submenu trigger: opens the submenu on its first item.                                                           |
| Arrow Left (Right in RTL) | In a submenu: closes it, back on its trigger.                                                                        |
| A character               | The next item whose text starts with it; characters typed within 750 ms add up, and Space among them is text.        |
| Escape                    | Closes one level: the submenu on top, or the menu. Focus goes back to its trigger.                                   |
| Tab, Shift+Tab            | Close the whole menu. Tab moves on from the trigger; Shift+Tab stays on it.                                          |

- **On open**, focus moves to the first item that can run (Arrow Up: the last one). Opened by a
  pointer, the popup itself takes focus and no item is highlighted until a key or the pointer
  picks one.
- **On close**, focus returns to the trigger without scrolling the page, after Escape, Tab, an
  item that ran or a click outside on nothing focusable; a click on a button or a field outside
  leaves focus there.
- **Running an item** closes the whole menu and returns focus before the item's `onClick` runs,
  so a handler that opens a dialog gets focus back on the trigger when it closes. Checkbox and
  radio items stay open.
- **Disabled items** (`aria-disabled`) stay in the arrow order and typeahead, as the pattern
  asks, but do not run.
- **The pointer** highlights the item under it, and leaving the items clears the highlight. A
  mouse press on the trigger opens the menu at once: releasing it on an item runs the item, and
  releasing it outside closes the menu. A submenu opens after the pointer rests 100 ms on its
  trigger, and stays open while the pointer heads for it across other items.
- **A click outside** closes the whole menu, submenus included, and a click in a menu closes the
  submenus open from it. A right-click, a middle click or a second finger outside leaves the menu
  open, as in Base UI.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger opens the popup with `popovertarget`, and Escape or a click outside closes it: a menu
in a server-rendered page opens before any script loads, and with none. Tab then moves through the
items in order, and links work; commands, which run JavaScript, need it anyway. `open`,
`onOpenChange` and the `bind:` props need the component to run in the browser, in an island.

The keyboard contract comes from a small script: a page that renders a `Menu` loads it once, as a
2.4 kB (brotli) module without the Lumiose runtime, and islands bundle it. It defines `lu-menu`,
which upgrades every menu on the page in place, and adds what the native popover lacks: focus on
open and its return on close, the arrows, Home, End and typeahead, Escape one level at a time, Tab,
submenus, checkbox and radio items, disabled items, `data-highlighted`, and the pointer behaviour
above. It also takes over dismissal: the popup becomes a manual popover when the script opens it,
and the script closes it on a click outside (main button only), on Escape, and on a close request
such as the Android back gesture. Until it loads (or without JavaScript) the menu behaves as a
native `popover="auto"` of buttons, which any click outside closes.

The element is also an API of its own, for scripts and other frameworks:

- `open`: a property; setting it to `true` or `false` opens or closes the menu.
- `openchange`: an event (not bubbling, like `toggle`) with `detail.open`, after the menu opens or
  closes.
- `checkedchange`: a bubbling event that checkbox and radio items fire with `detail.checked` when
  a click, Enter or Space checks or unchecks them.

## Browser support

- **Popovers and `popovertarget`**: Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17.
- **CSS anchor positioning** places the popup: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26
  (partly; 27 fully). Elsewhere the popup shows where the browser shows any popover, in the middle
  of the viewport, and still works.
- **`showPopover({ source })`**, which ties a popup the script opens to its trigger: Chrome 137,
  Firefox 144, Safari 26. Older browsers open it the same way.
- **`CloseWatcher`**, for the Android back gesture: Chrome 126, Firefox 149. Elsewhere Escape
  still closes the menu.
- **Exit animations** that keep the popup in the top layer while it fades (`overlay`) are
  Chromium-only.

- [Dialog](dialog.md): a menu item can open one; focus returns to the menu's trigger when it
  closes.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the
  browser, for `open`, `onOpenChange` and the `bind:` props.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `bind:`, native events with `on:` and
  `ref`.
